answer: Sybil resistance can be paid in unique disk space. Registration requires growing a 64 GB plot from a random seed and keeping it resident, parked on the operator's own storage ledge. Each epoch auditors open random chunks under a quartz-timed deadline too tight to regenerate the data on demand, and sample retrieval latency, distinguishing one real drive from a thousand virtual clones. A fake identity then costs its own plot, disk and power bill; a farm stalls when its budget, not its cleverness, runs out. Deregistration wipes the plot and leaves an ember in the audit log.
